contract: OS import models for frame_trace.py --snapshot and xlate.py. A snapshot run maps a loaded OS module's export entries on first call: an export listed here runs its model (its code is written at the entry); any other export is int3 and stops the run with its name. do values: return (mov rax, imm64; ret: the export returns value and has no other effect); memcpy (Win64 memcpy(dst, src, n): returns dst, copies n bytes forward); qpc (QueryPerformanceCounter: stores value at *rcx, returns TRUE); tls_get / tls_set (TlsGetValue / TlsSetValue on the thread's own TEB slots); tebread (returns the DWORD at gs:[offset], zero-extended: GetLastError). Keyed by module file name and export name. Each entry carries the evidence for its model; a wrong model is a divergence, not a default.

why: Called as the thunk at 0x1403FF444: call [0x14252F340]; xor eax,eax; add rsp,0x28; ret. The thunk discards the value, so the callee only has to return.
Model assumption: the replay runs one thread and never waits on the lock; a lock held by another thread at the snapshot instant is not represented.
Pair of RtlEnterCriticalSection; no waiters are modelled (see above).
Win64 memcpy(void *dst, const void *src, size_t n): rcx, rdx, r8; returns dst in rax.
Model assumption: non-overlapping source and destination (the memcpy contract); forward rep movsb.

Caller: the wait helper at 0x141B389D0 (CONFIRMED disassembly): WaitForSingleObject(handle, 0); if the result is 0 it returns 0 and the pump's drain loop at 0x141B3E146 runs again; any nonzero result exits the loop (0x18000001 for WAIT_TIMEOUT 0x102, 0x18000002 otherwise).

So a return of 0 (WAIT_OBJECT_0) would drain forever (2.5 M calls in the first pump frame, the reason for this value). 0x102 (WAIT_TIMEOUT, 258) ends the drain at once, so the pump dispatches the ring as it stands; pes-re-advance.md's emulated run reached the record loop with the same value.
Model assumption: no other thread signals the handle during the replay (the producers are not run). A wait is an OS boundary: named here, and each call is counted in the record under import_calls.

Caller: the pump's dispatch path (rets 0x1403dc579 .. 0x1403ff4aa in the first frame). The value is the replayed thread's id: the snapshot's main-thread TEB ClientId.Thread (+0x48), 36 = Wine's process id 32 + 4 (frame_trace.main_teb), CONFIRMED from the snapshot.
Model assumption: the replay runs as that thread. A replay of a different thread's TEB must change this value; it is not read from the TEB at run time (a stop would hide that).
The pump's time base (pes-re-advance.md): xmm2/xmm3 come from QueryPerformanceCounter via 0x141B34A30, in 10 MHz ticks (freq constant 0x1437F00F0 = 10,000,000, CONFIRMED in that doc).

MODEL, not evidence: the clock is frozen at 0 for every call, so the pump's frame delta is the accumulated value only. Frame timing from this run is therefore not PES's; it is labelled as a fixed-clock replay wherever it is reported.

Windows x64 semantics: TlsGetValue(index) returns TEB.TlsSlots[index] for index < 64 (TEB +0x1480); the slot is read from the replayed thread's own TEB (gs base = the snapshot TEB), so the game's TLS values are the snapshot's.
Model assumption: indices >= 64 (TlsExpansionSlots) are not modelled and return NULL; any such call is a named divergence to revisit.
Windows x64 semantics: TlsSetValue(index, value) stores TEB.TlsSlots[index] for index < 64 and returns TRUE; indices >= 64 return FALSE (not modelled).
The store is into the replay's own copy of the TEB page; it is part of the call-time delta, as any write.

Named by the recorded cutscene-create call (proc/seq008: unmodelled import kernelbase.dll!GetLastError at 0x6FFFFF3A9151). The slot 0x14252F328 is kernel32.dll!GetLastError (import_slots.json); kernel32 forwards it to kernelbase.

Windows x64 semantics: GetLastError returns the DWORD TEB.LastErrorValue. [INF] offset +0x68 is the standard x64 TEB layout (ClientId.Thread at +0x48 is confirmed for this snapshot in pes-re-import-slots.md); not read from a Windows header here.
Model assumption: no OS call in the replay sets the last error; the value is the snapshot's TEB (read from the replayed thread's own TEB, as TlsGetValue is).
The export the replay's loaded module resolves to (proc/seq008). Same model as kernel32.dll!GetLastError, which the translator keys on (the slot's module).

Wine ntdll RtlAcquireSRWLockShared (file offset 0x1d380, read from the prefix's ntdll.dll): the fast path is taken when the low word of the lock dword is zero; it adds 0x10000 (the shared count, high word) by lock cmpxchg, and returns with eax = old value, edx = old value, ecx = new value. The slow path (exclusive or waiting bits set) calls RtlWaitOnAddress, which a single-thread replay cannot model: the code here is int3, so such a case is excluded, never replayed wrong.
Model assumption: the replay is single-threaded, so the cmpxchg always succeeds (no contention). The captures seq013 and seq023 are the only callers in the replay set.

Wine ntdll RtlReleaseSRWLockShared (file offset 0x38360): the fast path is taken when the exclusive bit (bit 0) is clear and the shared count (high word) is nonzero; it stores lock - 0x10000 and returns with eax = old value, edx = count - 1, r8d = new value. Any other case (exclusive bit set, no shared holders: the waiter-wake path) is int3 here, excluded, never replayed wrong.
Model assumption: single-threaded replay, uncontended release.

Wine kernelbase FlsGetValue (file offset 0x218a0) calls ntdll RtlFlsGetValue(index, &value) and returns value with TEB+0x68 (LastErrorValue) = 0; on failure it sets TEB+0x68 = RtlNtStatusToDosError(status) and returns 0. Wine ntdll RtlFlsGetValue (file offset 0x29540) reads the FLS vector from TEB+0x17C8 (gs:[0x30] is the TEB self pointer), rejects index-1 > 0xFEE or a null vector with STATUS_INVALID_PARAMETER (0xC000000D), and walks blocks of 16<<k slots: value = block[k][rem+1] (0 when the block is null). The code here is that walk, inlined; the failure path writes 87 (ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER) to TEB+0x68 [INF: the standard STATUS_INVALID_PARAMETER -> ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER mapping; RtlNtStatusToDosError itself is not disassembled here].

Model assumption: the replay's TEB and FLS vector are the snapshot's own (the TEB and FlsData pages are read from the snapshot). The 0x17C8 offset is read from the Wine ntdll code, not from a Windows header.

Wine ntdll RtlSetLastWin32Error (file offset 0x39cb0, read from the prefix's ntdll.dll): mov rax, gs:[0x30]; mov [rax+0x68], ecx; ret. It stores the DWORD in TEB.LastErrorValue (TEB+0x68, the same slot as GetLastError) and returns nothing. rax is left as the TEB self pointer.
Reached from the recorded cutscene-create call (seq008) through the FlsGetValue failure path's SetLastError.

errno_t strcpy_s(char *dst, size_t size, const char *src): rcx, rdx, r8; returns errno_t in eax. Export 2383 (ordinal 2384) of the PES prefix's ucrtbase.dll (SizeOfImage 0xF4000, RVA 0x17E00), named by its export directory.

Behaviour read from the loaded DLL's code in the snapshot (live_seq085, 0x6FFFFEC77E00): dst or size zero -> EINVAL (0x16) with no write; src zero -> *dst = 0 then EINVAL; otherwise copy src to dst up to and including its NUL; if no NUL fits in size -> *dst = 0 and ERANGE (0x22, value 34); else 0.

ponytail: the model does not store errno (ucrtbase per-thread state, reached through _errno at RVA 0xA550) and does not call _invalid_parameter_noinfo (RVA 0x684C0). Neither is in the game's diffed memory; a game read of errno after strcpy_s is not modelled (OPEN).

void *memset(void *dst, int c, size_t n): rcx, edx, r8; returns dst in rax. Export of the PES prefix's VCRUNTIME140.dll (module name from its export directory), RVA 0x19A0 in a full capture (pid407792/seq001, 0x6FFFFB8219A0).

Contract: writes the low byte of c to n bytes at dst, returns dst, leaves rdi and rsi unchanged (Win64 callee-saved). The model is that contract, not the DLL's code: the DLL fills vectors (its first instructions build 0x0101010101010101 by movabs and imul, then punpcklbw), so the byte pattern is the same and the code differs.

Model: mov r9, rcx (dst kept); push rdi; mov rdi, rcx; mov eax, edx; mov rcx, r8; rep stosb; mov rax, r9; pop rdi; ret. n = 0 stores nothing. Checked by test_memset_model.py. The callers' argument shapes (44C880, 445E90) are not checked yet (OPEN).

void *memmove(void *dst, const void *src, size_t n): rcx, rdx, r8; returns dst in rax. Export of the PES prefix's VCRUNTIME140.dll at RVA 0x12F0 (the danger-writer replay stops at 0x6FFFFBC712F1 = base 0x6FFFFBC70000 + 0x12F1 with the module named by the snapshot's export directory; the IAT slot is 0x14252FD68, called from the lane-list insert 0x140A790AB).
Contract: copies n bytes as if through a temporary, returns dst, leaves rdi and rsi unchanged (Win64 callee-saved). The model is that contract, not the DLL's code (which is vectorised).

Model: mov rax, rcx; push rdi; push rsi; mov rdi, rcx; mov rsi, rdx; mov rcx, r8; if dst <= src or dst >= src + n copy forward (rep movsb), else copy backward from the last byte (std; rep movsb; cld); pop rsi; pop rdi; ret. rcx is 0 after the copy and r9 = src + n when dst > src. Checked by test_memmove_model.py; the C++ mirror (xlate.import_model_lines) is compared with it by snapdiff on the danger-writer captures.
